blocks.text: Your Mac is your primary office. If you use Chrome, you know the pain of having twenty tabs open for different carriers. Each tab represents a potential login issue or a lost document. You need a system to keep your browser from becoming a bottleneck.
Organizing Chrome for insurance agents on Mac

Start by using Chrome Profiles. If you work with multiple carriers, create a separate profile for each one. This keeps cookies and logins isolated. Go to your profile icon in the top right of Chrome, click Add, and set up a new space for that specific carrier. This prevents the common error where one portal logs you out because another carrier site refreshed.

items: Use ⌘ + T to open a new tab for a quick search.
Use ⌘ + Option + Right Arrow to move between your open tabs.
Use ⌘ + L to jump to the address bar and type a new URL immediately.
Use ⌘ + W to close the current tab when you finish a task.

blocks.text: Managing carrier portals and agency management systems

Many agency management systems like Applied Epic or AgencyBloc are web-based. They often have complex interfaces with small buttons. If you cannot find a specific form or report, do not waste time scanning the screen. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where the button is. Lazur will draw a circle around the exact field or menu item you need.

If a site is acting slow, it is often due to cached data. Go to Chrome > Settings > Privacy and security > Clear browsing data. Select the site from the list and clear only that data to avoid logging out of your other portals.
blocks.title: Fixing slow portals

blocks.text: You spend hours re-keying data from emails into your CRM. Stop doing this manually. Use Lazur to dictate notes directly into your browser forms. Hold fn and speak your client's policy details. Lazur types it out at your cursor location. This saves you from switching between your email and your browser constantly.
Common mistakes insurance agents make in Chrome

items: Keeping too many tabs open. It slows down your Mac and makes it harder to find the right carrier site.
Ignoring browser updates. Chrome updates often contain security patches that keep your client data safe.
Using the same password for every portal. Use a dedicated password manager instead.
Not pinning critical sites. Pin your most used portals to the tab bar by right-clicking the tab and choosing Pin.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you work faster

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It does not click for you, but it acts as a guide. When you are lost in a deep menu structure in a carrier portal, ask Lazur how to find the renewal report. It will walk you through the steps, one click at a time. This is better than hunting through help manuals.

You likely manage a high volume of email. Keep your inbox organized by using labels in Gmail. If you need to delegate access to an assistant, do it through the Gmail settings menu. When you need to send a quick link to a client, use the browser address bar to copy it quickly. If you are struggling to find a specific email thread, use the search operators in Gmail to filter by sender or subject.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons in my carrier portal?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points, guides, and answers questions out loud. It does not interact with your browser or click buttons for you.

faq.question: How do I speed up Chrome on my Mac?
faq.answer: Clear your cache, remove unused extensions, and keep your open tabs to a minimum. Using separate profiles for different carriers also helps.

faq.question: Is my data safe when using Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only sees your screen when you hold the shortcut. Audio and screenshots are not stored and are never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur is built for macOS. A Windows version is planned but not currently available.
